title: Medicare Card Phone Scam
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying you need a new card or that your benefits are at risk. They ask for your Medicare number or other personal information.
example_message: "Hello, this is Medicare. We need to send you a new card. Can you please confirm your Medicare number and date of birth?"
red_flags: Unsolicited call about your Medicare card
Threats that your benefits will end
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at the number on your card if you have concerns.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Up
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and need to call a number for help. The scammer pretends to be from Microsoft or Apple and tries to get access to your computer or asks for payment.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up warning with a phone number
Asked to give remote access to your computer
Asked to pay in gift cards or wire transfer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number or give anyone access to your computer.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer, saying your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They ask you to send cash or gift cards.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need bail money. Please don’t tell mom and dad. Can you send $2,000 right away?"
red_flags: Asked to pay by gift card or wire transfer
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member directly to check the story.

title: Social Security Text Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with your Social Security benefits and you must click a link or call a number. The scammers try to steal your information.
example_message: "Your Social Security account is suspended. Click here to reactivate: [fake link]"
red_flags: Links to click or numbers to call
what_to_do: Delete the text and do not click any links or call any numbers.

title: Romance Scam on Facebook
how_it_works: A scammer pretends to be a new friend or love interest on Facebook. After building trust, they ask for money for an emergency or travel.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need help. My wallet was stolen overseas and I need $1,500 to get home."
red_flags: Stories about emergencies or travel problems
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person, no matter how convincing their story.
